Synopsis:
    Brent crude is approaching $100/bbl driven by escalating Middle East conflict (Houthi strikes on Saudi cities, US-Iran confrontations). The yen is surging ~4% in September, pressuring carry trades. Markets are on edge ahead of US inflation data and central bank meetings (Fed + BOJ, Sept 17-18). BOJ expected to hike 25bps. Dollar is on the back foot; euro and sterling steady. The macro backdrop is one of rising energy costs and shifting rate expectations globally.

Q01. Is the content's main message about EU energy, EU commodities, German power market prices, German energy economics?
Relevance: NO — The article is focused on FX markets (JPY, USD), oil prices, and central bank policy (Fed, BOJ). EU/German energy is not addressed.

Q02. Is the content confirming already known information or reporting very new/uncertain risks?
Risk score: 55 — The Middle East escalation adds a new layer of uncertainty (Houthi strikes on Saudi cities, direct US-Iran confrontations), but rising oil and yen strength have been building themes. The inflation data and BOJ meeting as near-term pivots are already well-flagged. The specific military escalation steps are the main source of novelty.

Q03. Is the content explicit about bullish impact on the German power futures market?
Explicit: NO — German power futures are not mentioned. Indirectly, Brent pushing toward $100 carries a bullish read-through for gas and power prices in Europe, but this is not stated.
